batchName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE) - Medium Batch 1
chapterName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE)

questions.question: In 32 BC, the Senate formally declared war on whom?
options: Lepidus
Mark Antony
Parthia
Cleopatra
The king of Armenia
questions.explanation: The war was formally declared on Cleopatra, though everyone understood it to be against Antony.
questions.sourceQuote: In 32 BC the Senate declared war on Cleopatra, a war everyone understood to be against Antony.

questions.question: What happened when the triumvirate expired at the end of 33 BC?
options: Antony returned to Rome to stand for consul
Both consuls and hundreds of senators fled to Antony
Octavian was named dictator
Lepidus was recalled from exile
The Senate renewed it for five years
questions.explanation: Both consuls and hundreds of senators left Rome to join Antony, showing he still had powerful support in the propaganda war.
questions.sourceQuote: When the triumvirate expired at the end of 33 BC, both consuls and hundreds of senators fled Rome to join Antony.

questions.question: Whom did Octavian have killed, supposedly remarking that "two Caesars are one too many"?
options: The admiral who held Sicily
Antony's younger brother
The captive king of Armenia
Cleopatra's son by Julius Caesar
The exiled Lepidus
questions.explanation: Octavian removed Cleopatra's son by Julius Caesar, a rival claimant to Caesar's legacy. Egypt then became a Roman province.
questions.sourceQuote: Octavian had her son by Julius Caesar killed, supposedly remarking that "two Caesars are one too many".

questions.question: How did Antony's warships at Actium compare with Octavian's?
options: Mostly converted Egyptian merchant ships
Equal in size but far fewer in number
Huge and armoured, but slow and short of rowers
Smaller and nimbler, crewed by veterans
Faster but lightly built and unarmoured
questions.explanation: Antony's galleys were huge and armoured but slow. Octavian's smaller, nimble ships darted in to shower their decks with arrows and stones.
questions.sourceQuote: His galleys were huge and armoured, but slow and short of rowers.

questions.question: Ancient writers claimed Cleopatra manipulated Antony. How do modern historians explain the relationship?
options: He was strengthening a useful client ally
He was ordered to court her by the Senate
He needed her treasury to pay off Octavian
She charmed him with Egyptian magic
He hoped to become king of Egypt
questions.explanation: Modern historians see the alliance as part of Antony's policy of backing strong client monarchs, not as manipulation.
questions.sourceQuote: Modern historians think he was simply strengthening a useful ally, in line with his policy of backing strong client monarchs.

questions.question: Who were the equites, many of whom died in the proscriptions?
options: The elected tribunes of the people
Freed slaves employed as informers
Caesar's veteran cavalry officers
The wealthy class just below the senators
The priests of the war god Mars
questions.explanation: The equites, or knights, were the wealthy class just below the senators. Ancient estimates of proscription victims include many knights alongside senators.
questions.sourceQuote: Ancient writers give figures ranging from about 130 senators to 300 men, plus many knights (*equites*), the wealthy class just below the senators.

questions.question: Why did Antony and Octavian not fight when they faced each other at Brundisium in 40 BC?
options: Parthia had just invaded the east
Lepidus threatened to attack them both
Their soldiers refused to fight each other
A storm wrecked Antony's fleet
The Senate ordered a truce
questions.explanation: The soldiers refused to fight one another and pushed their leaders to negotiate, producing the Treaty of Brundisium.
questions.sourceQuote: Their soldiers refused to fight one another and pushed them to negotiate.

questions.question: According to a story told about the first battle at Philippi, where did Octavian spend the fight?
options: Sick in bed in Rome
Aboard a ship offshore
Guarding the camp gates
Leading a cavalry charge
Hiding in a marsh
questions.explanation: It was said that Octavian hid in a marsh while one of the assassins' armies stormed his camp and destroyed three of his legions.
questions.sourceQuote: Octavian, it was said, spent the fight hiding in a marsh.

questions.question: What do some modern historians argue about Cleopatra's and Antony's escape from the fighting at Actium?
options: It was caused by sudden panic
A shift in the wind forced it
Antony was badly wounded
Cleopatra was betraying Antony
The breakout was the plan all along
questions.explanation: Ancient writers called it panic or betrayal, but some modern historians think breaking out was the plan. Most of the fleet was left behind.
questions.sourceQuote: Some modern historians argue the breakout was the plan all along.

questions.question: What honour did Julius Caesar officially receive in January 42 BC, before the Philippi campaign?
options: His ashes were moved to Alexandria
He was officially declared a god
His statue was placed among the kings
He was named father of the fatherland
He was reburied in the Senate house
questions.explanation: Caesar was officially declared a god in January 42 BC. His avengers then went to war against his assassins.
questions.sourceQuote: In January 42 BC Julius Caesar was officially declared a god.
